_comment: MCP permission policy for mcp-guard.sh. Globs match against the full tool_name (e.g. mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__execute_sql). Default for any tool NOT listed = allow + PostToolUse logging. The always-on content sentinel (credential-path / known-secret / curl-@file exfil) runs on ALL mcp tools (hardened 2026-06-12 F4 — no longer name-gated).

_require_token_notes.C3_code_exec: C3 (HIGH) — ungated arbitrary code-exec tools. ctx_execute / ctx_execute_file run arbitrary Python/JS/shell code in a subprocess and can read files, exfiltrate env-vars, or pivot to the host FS. Token-gating means the operator must physically confirm within 60s before any code executes. Kept in non_egress_servers because they do NOT open a network socket themselves — the egress gate is about outbound destinations, not write-risk.
_require_token_notes.C3b_destructive_writers: C3 (HIGH) — destructive LSP vault / symbol writers. These tools can overwrite symbol bodies, rename symbols project-wide, permanently delete them, or destroy/move Obsidian vault notes. All are irreversible without git history. Serena operates on any open project; engraph writes the live SecondBrain vault. Token gate ensures each destructive write has an explicit operator confirmation.
_require_token_notes._comment_skipping: The _comment_* strings in require_token are filtered by match_any() in mcp-guard.sh (case: _comment*) so they never match a real tool name and never cause false positives.

_egress_comment: Destination-aware egress control (Phase 1, Cross-Provider Egress Guard). default=deny applies ONLY to tools matching a network mode below; all other tools keep default-allow. Modes, checked in order: Mode 1 url_tools (host extracted from tool_input, must match allow_hosts), then non_egress_servers (localhost/fs-local — skip the gate), then Mode 2 connector_tools (allow iff full name matches an allow_connectors glob), then Mode 3 network_name_globs (fail-closed deny), then Mode 4 (hardened 2026-06-12 F5: unknown non-local tool carrying a scheme://host in its payload → fail-closed). Codex reads this same block live and fails closed. Hostnames + tool-name globs only; no secrets. See THREAT-MODEL-FREEZE.md.
_sensitive_paths_comment: Home-anchored credential paths + project-secret basenames denied to read-like commands on BOTH harnesses (CC protect-sensitive-reads.sh, Codex pre_tool_use_dispatch.py). Segment names only — no secrets. Both guards fall back to a built-in list if this block is missing (fail-safe, never fail-open). Read fresh per call; no restart.
